- Docs strongly advise `autoDeployTrigger: off`.

**Next.js with pnpm**
- The official guide only shows yarn: build `yarn; yarn build`, start `yarn start` (https://render.com/docs/deploy-nextjs-app).
- A search summary says Render docs list `pnpm install` as an example build command, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm build` and `pnpm start` are the likely equivalents. I did not find this on a fetched page.
- Node version, in priority order: `NODE_VERSION` env var, `.node-version`, `.nvmrc`, `engines`. The default for new services is `24.21.0` (https://render.com/docs/node-version).
- pnpm version pinning: the only source is an undated feedback thread suggesting `SKIP_INSTALL_DEPS=true` with `corepack enable; pnpm install; pnpm build` (https://feedback.render.com/features/p/support-corepack).

**DEV challenge** (https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-weekend-2026-10-01)
- Build window is Oct 2 02:00 UTC to **Oct 5 06:59 UTC**; winners are announced the week of Oct 5.
- It must be a brand-new project with open-source AI at its core, built for one real person, and the post must explain "why open innovation matters for what you built".
- Prizes: Overall $250 plus DEV++ and a badge. Categories at $200 each: Best Use of Render, Best Use of TabPFN, Best Use of Tinker, and a Qualcomm category (details truncated). The search snippet says $2,450 across 17 winners.
- Judging order: writing quality (weighted most), relevance, creativity, technical execution, partner tech (optional).
- Credits: "Several partners are giving participants credits and promo codes, including Tinker, Render, Backboard, and ElevenLabs. Claim yours at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos."
- ElevenLabs and Sentry are not listed as prize categories.

## 2. ElevenLabs

**TTS** (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert)
- `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}` with header `xi-api-key`.
- Defaults are `eleven_multilingual_v2` and `mp3_44100_128`.
- SDK is `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`: `new ElevenLabsClient({ apiKey })`, then `client.textToSpeech.convert(voiceId, { text, modelId, outputFormat })`.

**Models** (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)
- Low latency: `eleven_v4_turbo` (~100 ms) is the recommended one; `eleven_flash_v2_5` (~75 ms) is the faster alternative.
- Also current: `eleven_v4`, `eleven_v3`, `eleven_v3_conversational`.
- Deprecated: `eleven_turbo_v2_5` (use `eleven_flash_v2_5`) and `scribe_v1` (use `scribe_v2`).

**Voices**
- List them with `GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v2/voices?category=premade&voice_type=default`; the response has `voice_id`, `name`, `labels`, `description`, `preview_url` (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/voices/search).
- No verified pair of IDs. A search summary says the defaults were renamed (Sarah to "Talia - Warm Soft Guide", George to "Eldrin - Crisp British Baritone", Bill to "Wyatt - Seasoned Mentor"). Query the endpoint and pick by `labels`.
- `JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb` is the ID in the official docs example; the docs do not name the voice.

**Speech-to-text** (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert, https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/speech-to-text)
- `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/speech-to-text` with `model_id: "scribe_v2"`.
- `words[]` items: `text`, `start`, `end`, `type` (`word`, `spacing`, `audio_event`), `logprob`, optional `speaker_id`.
- Other params: `timestamps_granularity` (`word` or `character`), `tag_audio_events`, `diarize`.
- Filler words: `no_verbatim`: "If true, the transcription will not have any filler words, false starts and non-speech sounds. Only supported with scribe_v2 model". So fillers are kept unless you set it; the docs imply that default but do not state it.

**Free tier**
- "10k credits per month", no commercial licence (https://elevenlabs.io/pricing).
- API access on free: yes per search snippets of help.elevenlabs.io, which also put STT at about 330 credits per minute (roughly 30 minutes a month if you spend nothing on TTS). Neither was confirmed on a fetched page.

## 3. Sentry

**Setup** (https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/)
- `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`
- Creates or modifies: `instrumentation-client.ts`, `sentry.server.config.ts`, `sentry.edge.config.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`, `app/global-error.tsx`, `next.config.ts` (wrapped in `withSentryConfig`), `app/sentry-example-page/page.tsx`, `app/api/sentry-example-api/route.ts`, `.env.sentry-build-plugin`.

**Vercel AI integration** (https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/configuration/integrations/vercelai/)
- `Sentry.vercelAIIntegration()` is on by default when tracing is enabled.
- Options: `Sentry.vercelAIIntegration({ recordInputs: false, recordOutputs: false })`; both default to `true`.

Research complete. Two findings change the likely design: Entire no longer stores checkpoints on a branch by default, and Mastra is now on AI SDK v7.

## Part A: Mastra

**1. Versions**
- `@mastra/core` is 1.74.0 and requires Node `>=22.13.0` (https://registry.npmjs.org/@mastra/core/latest).
- It bundles `@ai-sdk/provider` v5, v6 and v7 side by side; the Next.js guide uses `version: 'v7'`, and `ai` latest is 7.0.127 (https://mastra.ai/guides/getting-started/next-js).
- Zod peer range is `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`.

**2. Ollama / custom OpenAI-compatible URL**
- The built-in model router is the documented route for local models (https://mastra.ai/models):
  ```ts
  import { Agent } from "@mastra/core/agent";
  const agent = new Agent({
    id: "my-agent", name: "My Agent", instructions: "You are a helpful assistant",
    model: { id: "custom/my-qwen3-model", url: "http://your-custom-openai-compatible-endpoint.com/v1" }
  })
  ```
- Docs say `url` must be the base URL, not the chat endpoint, and that `provider/model` form sends a bare model name. `apiKey` and `headers` are also accepted on the object; `api: "responses"` is opt-in and Chat Completions is the default.
- So for Ollama it would be `{ id: "ollama/<gemma tag>", url: "http://localhost:11434/v1" }`. This is my inference: the docs only show LM Studio (`lmstudio/...`, `http://localhost:1234/v1`).
- Mastra's Ollama page instead says `pnpm add ollama-ai-provider-v2` and shows no code (https://mastra.ai/models/providers/ollama). That package is 4.0.1 with peers `ai ^7.0.0` and `zod ^4.0.16`.
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` is 3.0.62; I did not find a Mastra doc snippet using it.

**3. `createTool`** (https://mastra.ai/reference/tools/create-tool)
```ts
import { createTool } from '@mastra/core/tools'
createTool({ id, description, inputSchema: z.object({...}), outputSchema: z.object({...}),
  execute: async (input, context) => output })
```
- `input` is the validated input directly, not wrapped in `{ context }`.
- `context` carries `requestContext`, `abortSignal`, `agent`, `workflow`, `mcp`, `observe`.

**4. Structured output** (https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/structured-output)
- `const res = await agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema } })`, then read `res.object`.
- `jsonPromptInjection`: `false` (native), `'inline'`, `true`/`'system'`, or `'auto'` (prompt injection for models without native support).
- `model`: a separate structuring model.
- `errorStrategy`: `'strict'` (default, throws), `'warn'`, or `'fallback'` with `fallbackValue`.
- `instructions`: a compact description injected instead of the schema.

**5. Memory**
- Install `@mastra/memory` (1.35.0) and `@mastra/libsql` (1.25.0) (https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/overview).
- Storage: `new LibSQLStore({ id: 'mastra-storage', url: 'file:./storage.db' })` (https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/libsql).
- Per call: `agent.generate(msg, { memory: { resource: 'user-123', thread: 'conversation-123' } })`.
- Working memory: `new Memory({ storage, options: { workingMemory: { enabled: true, scope: 'resource', template } } })`, with `template` or `schema` but not both (https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory).
- File storage does not work on serverless platforms with ephemeral filesystems.
- Relative `file:` paths have a reported Next.js path issue (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/4507); I saw only the title, so use an absolute path to be safe.
- Missing `@libsql/win32-x64-msvc` binary errors on Windows are reported in other libsql projects, not Mastra specifically (https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/issues/1797, https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/issues/9860).

**6. Adding to Next.js**
- The guide uses `pnpm dlx mastra@latest init`, which creates `src/mastra/index.ts`, `agents/` and `tools/`.
- Then `pnpm add @mastra/ai-sdk@latest @ai-sdk/react ai`; the route handler uses `handleChatStream({ mastra, agentId, version: 'v7', params })`.
- Optional: `@mastra/next` plus `hono` to mount Mastra's full HTTP API.
- `serverExternalPackages: ['@mastra/*']` in `next.config.ts` is documented for Vercel deployment (https://mastra.ai/docs/deployment/web-framework). The getting-started guide does not mention it.

**7. Sentry**
- Official exporter `@mastra/sentry` 1.2.23, with `@mastra/observability` (https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/tracing/exporters/sentry):
  ```ts
  observability: new Observability({ configs: { sentry: { serviceName: 'my-service',
    exporters: [ new SentryExporter({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN!, environment: 'production', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }) ] } } })
  ```
- Sentry's own `Sentry.vercelAIIntegration({ recordInputs, recordOutputs })` is on by default when tracing is configured, Node runtime only (not Edge), and supports `ai` `>=3.0.0 <=7` (https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/configuration/integrations/vercelai/).

# Viva: Phase 0 plan (setup, research, spikes)

## Context

Viva is a weekend-challenge build (deadline Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST). Phase 0 has a 3 h timebox and exists to remove the risks that could sink the architecture before real coding starts: can a ~4B Gemma on a 16 GB laptop do tool calls and structured output through Mastra, what do Entire checkpoints actually look like, and which hosted Gemma do we compare against. No code has been written; the repo has only `CLAUDE.md`, `PRD.md`, `PHASES.md` (untracked, at the root) and no commits.

## 1. What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain** (local on Ollama, a larger Gemma hosted for the Render demo and comparison); **Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory of weak spots. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold the repo, turn on session capture (Entire, DevRelay), pick the models, run two spikes (Mastra + small Gemma, Entire format), read partner docs, benchmark local vs hosted, and collect fixtures. Its output is decisions in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, not features.

## 2. Research findings (checked today; items marked ⚠ need confirming when we run them)

### Local machine (measured)
- Node **22.11.0**, pnpm 10.33.4, Ollama 0.35.1 (no models pulled), Entire CLI 0.11.3 (not enabled here), Docker, Go, `gh` logged in as AbdulWasih05.
- 15.9 GB RAM, NVIDIA MX130 (small VRAM, so mostly CPU inference).
- Remote `AbdulWasih05/Viva` exists, public, empty, created 2026-10-03 (inside the window). Local branch is `master`; CLAUDE context says main branch is `main`.

### Gemma
- **Gemma 4 is current** (E2B, E4B = 4.5B effective, 12B, 26B, 31B; Apache 2.0; native system role and function calling).
- Ollama tag **`gemma4:e4b`**: badges vision, **tools**, thinking, audio; Q4_K_M; 128K context. ⚠ Download size was reported as 6.6 GB by one page and 9.5 GB by another; confirm at pull time.
- Fallback tags: `gemma4:e2b` (~4.6 GB), then `gemma3:4b` (3.3 GB, **no tools badge**, would need tools driven by deterministic code).
- Ollama defaults to a **4k context** on this machine; raise with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (the `/v1` endpoint cannot set `num_ctx` per request). `tool_choice` is not supported on Ollama's `/v1`.
- Images are accepted by all Gemma 4 sizes, so Phase 8 is possible.

### Hosted larger Gemma
- **Google AI Studio / Gemini API:** `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, free, system instructions + function calling supported. ⚠ Rate limits unpublished; JSON mode for Gemma and Gemma via the OpenAI-compatible base URL (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) not confirmed in docs.
- **OpenRouter:** `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`, tools + `response_format` listed; 20 RPM, 50 req/day (1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **DeepInfra:** `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, $0.15 / $0.40 per 1M tokens (paid fallback).

### Mastra
- `@mastra/core` 1.74.0, **requires Node >= 22.13.0** (we have 22.11.0, must upgrade). Uses AI SDK v7; zod 3.25+ or 4.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via the built-in model router: `model: { id: "<provider>/<model>", url: "<base url>/v1", apiKey? }`. ⚠ Docs show LM Studio only; the Ollama form is inferred. Fallback: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (`createOpenAICompatible`).
- `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, context) => ... })`.
- Structured output: `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`, read `res.object`.
- Memory: `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`, `new LibSQLStore({ id, url: "file:..." })`, per call `memory: { resource, thread }`. Use an absolute file path (a relative-path issue under Next.js is reported).
- Sentry: official `@mastra/sentry` exporter exists (with `@mastra/observability`).

### Entire (differs from what PHASES.md assumed in places)
- Default backend is **one git ref per checkpoint**: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (not a branch). Tree: `metadata.json`, `0/prompt.txt`, `0/full.jsonl`, `0/transcript.jsonl`, `0/metadata.json`.
- Root `metadata.json` has `files_touched`, `sessions[]`, `token_usage`. Commits get trailers `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` and `Entire-Attribution: 73% agent (146/200 lines)`. So file-level provenance is available; attribution is per commit, ⚠ per-line data not confirmed.
- Refs are pushed on `git push` by default and are **readable via GitHub REST** (`git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs) on public repos; verified by the research agent on `entireio/cli`.
- The command is **`entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`**; a top-level `entire explain` is not in the CLI help. Docs wording gets corrected in DECISIONS.md.
- Secrets are redacted best-effort before a checkpoint is written; transcripts on a public repo are public.

### Render / ElevenLabs / Sentry (read only, used in Phases 5 to 7)
- **Render:** private services and disks are **paid only**. An 8 GB instance (`4c-8g`) is roughly $175/mo by third-party pricing, about $17 for 3 days ⚠ (official price page did not load). Free web service spins down after 15 min. Deploy button: `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`. No official Ollama template found.
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; STT `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` with `text/start/end/type`. Filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set (good for delivery coaching). Free tier 10k credits/month ⚠ STT burns about 330 credits/min by an unconfirmed snippet. Voice IDs to be picked via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default (set `recordInputs/recordOutputs: false` for privacy); manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent` / `gen_ai.chat` / `gen_ai.execute_tool` with `span.setAttribute`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.

## 3. Plan for tasks 0.1 to 0.8

Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

# Viva: Phase 0 plan (setup, research, spikes), revision 2

## Context

Viva is a weekend-challenge build (deadline Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST). Phase 0 removes the risks that could sink the architecture before real coding starts. No code exists yet; the repo has only `CLAUDE.md`, `PRD.md`, `PHASES.md` (untracked, at the root) and no commits.

Revision 2 applies Wasih's review: hosted Gemma becomes the main model, the benchmark and fixtures shrink, Render cut item 3 is applied now, and the Next.js + LibSQL bundling risk is tested through a real API route.

## Decisions locked in this revision (all go to `docs/DECISIONS.md`)

1. **Main model = hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it` on Google AI Studio) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so `gemma4:e4b` runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` is the fallback.
2. **Local Gemma (`gemma4:e4b`) is used only for** the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` default becomes `hosted`; local mode still works by switching the env var.
3. **Render: cut item 3 applied now.** The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy button stay; no private Ollama service or disk. If partner credits cover it, use a paid Starter instance so a judge does not hit the free tier's cold start (free web services sleep after 15 minutes idle).
4. **Benchmark:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; the rest of the measuring folds into Phase 1 evals.
5. **Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself.
6. **Structured output fallback on Ollama:** if `/v1` JSON output is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field, not prompt tricks.
7. **Prize categories confirmed by Wasih** from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each). The cut order's "never cut" list stands.
8. **ElevenLabs:** claim promo credits first; real voice is used only for testing and the video (free 10k credits is roughly 30 minutes of speech-to-text at the unconfirmed 330 credits/min figure).
9. Rename `master` to `main`; move `PRD.md` and `PHASES.md` into `docs/`. Node goes to the current 22 LTS.

These change PRD F7 and CLAUDE.md wording ("local ~4B is the default brain"). Both docs get a short edit in 0.1 so they match.

## What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain; Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold, session capture, model wiring, two spikes (Mastra, Entire format), a small benchmark, fixtures. Its output is decisions, not features.

## Research findings (⚠ = confirm when we run it)

- **Machine:** Node 22.11.0 (too old for Mastra), pnpm 10.33.4, Ollama 0.35.1 with no models, Entire CLI 0.11.3 not enabled, `gh` logged in as AbdulWasih05, 15.9 GB RAM, MX130. Remote `AbdulWasih05/Viva` is public and empty.
- **Gemma 4** is current. `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama: tools, vision, thinking; 128K context; ⚠ size reported as 6.6 GB and 9.5 GB. Ollama defaults to a 4k context here; raise with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`. Ollama `/v1` has no `tool_choice`.
- **Hosted:** AI Studio serves `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, free, with system instructions and function calling. ⚠ Rate limits unpublished; JSON mode for Gemma and Gemma on the OpenAI-compatible URL (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) unconfirmed. OpenRouter free tier: 20 RPM, 50 req/day (1000/day after $10 credit).
- **Mastra:** `@mastra/core` 1.74.0, Node >= 22.13, AI SDK v7. Custom endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (⚠ only shown for LM Studio); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, context) => ... })`. Structured output via `structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue }`. Memory: `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`, `memory: { resource, thread }`. Official `@mastra/sentry` exporter exists.
- **Entire:** one git ref per checkpoint at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`; tree has `metadata.json` (`files_touched`, `sessions[]`), `0/prompt.txt`, `0/full.jsonl`. Commit trailers `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution` (per-commit percentage; ⚠ per-line data unconfirmed). Refs are pushed with `git push` and readable via GitHub REST `git/matching-refs`. The command is `entire checkpoint explain`, not `entire explain`. Secrets redacted best-effort; transcripts are public on a public repo.
- **Render:** private services and disks are paid only. Deploy button `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`. ⚠ Official prices did not load.
- **ElevenLabs:** `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS `eleven_flash_v2_5`; STT `scribe_v2` with `words[]` (`text/start/end/type`); fillers kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` on by default (set `recordInputs/recordOutputs: false`); manual `gen_ai.*` spans with `span.setAttribute`. Free plan 5M spans.

## Plan for tasks 0.1 to 0.8

Entire is enabled before the first commit so the scaffold commit is linked.

### 0.1 Repo and tooling
1. Wasih upgrades Node: `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` (22 LTS, >= 22.13). Verify `node --version`.
2. `git branch -M main`.
3. Scaffold in the scratchpad and copy in (the folder name has a capital letter and existing files, which `create-next-app` rejects): `pnpm create next-app@latest viva --ts --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*" --use-pnpm` (confirm flags with `--help`), copy all but `.git`, set `"name": "viva"`.
4. `pnpm add zod`; `pnpm add -D vitest tsx`.
5. Scripts: `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`, `test: vitest run`, `eval: tsx scripts/eval.ts`, `bench: tsx scripts/bench-models.ts`. One trivial Vitest test.
6. Move `PRD.md`, `PHASES.md` to `docs/`. Create `docs/PROGRESS.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` (with the locked decisions above), `docs/post/.gitkeep`, `.env.example`; add `.env`, `.viva/`, `.mastra/` to `.gitignore`. Update CLAUDE.md Commands, and the model wording in CLAUDE.md and PRD F7 to match decisions 1 to 3. Strike through (not delete) the PHASES.md lines that the decisions replace (5.1 private service, 0.7 run counts, 0.8 repo count).
7. Verify `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`. Commit `chore: scaffold Next.js app with tooling`; `git push -u origin main`.

### 0.2 Session capture (20 min timebox)
- `entire enable --agent claude-code`; set commit linking to "always" (exact flag from `entire configure --help`). Hooks land in `.claude/settings.json`, so the Claude Code session probably needs a restart.
- Verify after the first commit: `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`.
- Wasih runs the DevRelay installer himself (`iwr -useb https://devrelay.com/install.ps1 | iex`) and logs into Entire only if a command asks.
- Privacy rule into DECISIONS.md.

### 0.3 Gemma wiring
- **Hosted first:** Wasih creates the AI Studio key and puts it in `.env` (`HOSTED_BASE_URL`, `HOSTED_API_KEY`, `HOSTED_MODEL=gemma-4-31b-it`). One `curl` chat call to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plus one with `response_format` JSON and one with a tool, to learn what Gemma supports there. If Gemma is not served on that URL, switch to OpenRouter.
- **Local, in the background:** `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`, `ollama show gemma4:e4b`, set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192`, one timed prompt with `ollama ps` for tokens/sec and RAM. This number is post material for the "honest trade-offs" section.

### 0.4 Mastra spike (45 min, decides architecture)
- `pnpm add @mastra/core @mastra/memory @mastra/libsql` (add `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` only if the model-router form fails).
- `next.config.ts`: `serverExternalPackages: ["@libsql/client", "@mastra/*"]` from the start, since LibSQL is a native module.
- Script `scripts/spikes/mastra.ts` (run with `pnpm tsx`), against the **hosted** model, pass/fail counts over 5 runs each:
  1. plain `agent.generate`
  2. a `readFile` stub tool is called
  3. `structuredOutput` with a small zod schema
- **Memory is tested through a real route**, not only a script: a throwaway `src/app/api/spike-memory/route.ts` that saves and recalls a value with `LibSQLStore` at an absolute `.viva/memory.db` path. Check it under `pnpm dev` across a server restart, and again under `pnpm build` + `pnpm start`. The route is deleted once the result is logged.
- One quick local pass of checks 2 and 3 on `gemma4:e4b` (1 or 2 runs each) only to record whether it works; if `/v1` JSON is flaky, try Ollama's native `format` field and note the result.
- Decision recorded: how tools and structured output are wired on hosted, and what the local path falls back to.

### 0.5 Entire format spike (30 min)
- `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`, `git ls-tree -r <ref>`, `git show <ref>:metadata.json`, `git show <ref>:0/prompt.txt`, `git log -1 --format=%B`, `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`.
- After push: `gh api repos/AbdulWasih05/Viva/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then one tree and one blob call.
- Document where prompt, transcript, changed files and attribution live, and whether line-level data exists.

### 0.6 Partner research
- Done; findings and links copied into DECISIONS.md. Wasih claims Render and ElevenLabs credits at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos before any voice testing.

### 0.7 Model benchmark (small)
- `scripts/bench-models.ts`: one brief prompt + one question prompt on a small fixture; **3 local runs, 5 hosted runs**.
- Records structured-output validity, median latency, and whether the question names a real file; into PROGRESS.md tagged `[POST]` with run counts stated. Set `OLLAMA_MODEL` and `HOSTED_MODEL`.

### 0.8 Fixtures
- **2 public repos** of different shapes (one Wasih's own if public), snapshot of the files the ingest heuristic would select into `fixtures/<name>/` with a `SOURCE.md` (URL, commit SHA, licence).
- Third fixture is Viva itself, taken in Phase 3 once it has checkpoints.

### Close out
- Tick `docs/PHASES.md`, append to `docs/PROGRESS.md` (what changed, how verified, `[POST]` lines, a short "How it works"), commit per subtask.

## Wasih's to-do list today (not code)

- **Book the friend for tonight's test** (Phase 9) and check whether their repo is public; hosted mode reads public GitHub repos only, so a private repo means running Viva on their folder locally.
- Upgrade Node; create the AI Studio key (and an OpenRouter key as fallback) in `.env`.
- Claim Render and ElevenLabs credits; run the DevRelay installer.
- Tell me which of your public repos to use as a fixture.

## Accounts, keys and money

| Item | Needed for | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Node 22 LTS | Mastra | free, admin install |
| Google AI Studio key | main model | free |
| OpenRouter key | fallback | free at 50 req/day; $10 lifts to 1000/day |
| DEV account + DevRelay | agent session embed | free |
| hacktoberfest.com promos | Render, ElevenLabs credits | free, login |
| Render Starter instance | always-on demo | only if credits cover it; else free tier with cold start |
| ElevenLabs key | Phase 6 | promo credits; free tier is about 30 min of STT |
| Sentry DSN | Phase 7 | free |

Nothing in Phase 0 costs money.

## Still open (for Wasih)

1. Which public repo of yours becomes a fixture?
2. Is the friend's repo public?

## Verification (end of Phase 0)

- `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build` pass.
- `entire checkpoint list` shows a checkpoint for at least one commit, and the GitHub API returns the same ref.
- Mastra spike prints pass/fail counts on hosted Gemma for generate, tool call and structured output; the memory route returns the saved value after a restart in both dev and production builds.
- `pnpm bench` prints validity, median latency and real-file rate for both models, with run counts.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` holds the locked decisions, provider wiring, Entire format and hosted limits; Phase 0 boxes ticked.

## Context

Viva is a weekend-challenge build (deadline Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST). ## 1. What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain** (local on Ollama, a larger Gemma hosted for the Render demo and comparison); **Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory of weak spots. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold the repo, turn on session capture (Entire, DevRelay), pick the models, run two spikes (Mastra + small Gemma, Entire format), read partner docs, benchmark local vs hosted, and collect fixtures. Its output is decisions in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, not features.

Revision 2 applies Wasih's review: hosted Gemma becomes the main model, the benchmark and fixtures shrink, Render cut item 3 is applied now, and the Next.js + LibSQL bundling risk is tested through a real API route.

## Decisions locked in this revision (all go to `docs/DECISIONS.md`)

1. **Main model = hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it` on Google AI Studio) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so `gemma4:e4b` runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` is the fallback.
2. **Local Gemma (`gemma4:e4b`) is used only for** the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` default becomes `hosted`; local mode still works by switching the env var.
3. **Render: cut item 3 applied now.** The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy button stay; no private Ollama service or disk. If partner credits cover it, use a paid Starter instance so a judge does not hit the free tier's cold start (free web services sleep after 15 minutes idle).
4. **Benchmark:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; the rest of the measuring folds into Phase 1 evals.
5. **Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself.
6. **Structured output fallback on Ollama:** if `/v1` JSON output is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field, not prompt tricks.
7. **Prize categories confirmed by Wasih** from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each). The cut order's "never cut" list stands.
8. **ElevenLabs:** claim promo credits first; real voice is used only for testing and the video (free 10k credits is roughly 30 minutes of speech-to-text at the unconfirmed 330 credits/min figure).
9. Rename `master` to `main`; move `PRD.md` and `PHASES.md` into `docs/`. Node goes to the current 22 LTS.

These change PRD F7 and CLAUDE.md wording ("local ~4B is the default brain"). Both docs get a short edit in 0.1 so they match.

## What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain; Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold, session capture, model wiring, two spikes (Mastra, Entire format), a small benchmark, fixtures. Its output is decisions, not features.

## Research findings (⚠ = confirm when we run it)

- **Machine:** Node 22.11.0 (too old for Mastra), pnpm 10.33.4, Ollama 0.35.1 with no models, Entire CLI 0.11.3 not enabled, `gh` logged in as AbdulWasih05, 15.9 GB RAM, MX130. Remote `AbdulWasih05/Viva` is public and empty.
- **Gemma 4** is current. `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama: tools, vision, thinking; 128K context; ⚠ size reported as 6.6 GB and 9.5 GB. Ollama defaults to a 4k context here; raise with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`. Ollama `/v1` has no `tool_choice`.
- **Hosted:** AI Studio serves `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, free, with system instructions and function calling. ⚠ Rate limits unpublished; JSON mode for Gemma and Gemma on the OpenAI-compatible URL (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) unconfirmed. OpenRouter free tier: 20 RPM, 50 req/day (1000/day after $10 credit).
- **Mastra:** `@mastra/core` 1.74.0, Node >= 22.13, AI SDK v7. Custom endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (⚠ only shown for LM Studio); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, context) => ... })`. Structured output via `structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue }`. Memory: `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`, `memory: { resource, thread }`. Official `@mastra/sentry` exporter exists.
- **Entire:** one git ref per checkpoint at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`; tree has `metadata.json` (`files_touched`, `sessions[]`), `0/prompt.txt`, `0/full.jsonl`. Commit trailers `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution` (per-commit percentage; ⚠ per-line data unconfirmed). Refs are pushed with `git push` and readable via GitHub REST `git/matching-refs`. The command is `entire checkpoint explain`, not `entire explain`. Secrets redacted best-effort; transcripts are public on a public repo.
- **Render:** private services and disks are paid only. Deploy button `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`. ⚠ Official prices did not load.
- **ElevenLabs:** `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS `eleven_flash_v2_5`; STT `scribe_v2` with `words[]` (`text/start/end/type`); fillers kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` on by default (set `recordInputs/recordOutputs: false`); manual `gen_ai.*` spans with `span.setAttribute`. Free plan 5M spans.

Entire is enabled before the first commit so the scaffold commit is linked.

1. Wasih upgrades Node: `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` (22 LTS, >= 22.13). Verify `node --version`.

7. Verify `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`. Commit `chore: scaffold Next.js app with tooling`; `git push -u origin main`.

# Which model the app talks to. "hosted" is the default for development and the demo;
# "ollama" is for offline / private use on your own machine.

# DECISIONS

Architecture choices and research surprises, newest at the bottom. One line of reason each. Items marked "unverified" are from docs or third parties and have not been run by us yet.

## Phase 0 (4 Oct 2026)

### Models

- **D1. Main model is hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it`, Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the laptop's MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so a local Gemma runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. Fallback: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **D2. Local Gemma is `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama**, used for the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark only. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` defaults to `hosted`; switching the env var to `ollama` still runs everything locally.

## Phase 0: Setup, research, spikes (Sat, 3 h)

- [ ] **0.1 Repo and tooling**
  - [ ] Create public GitHub repo `viva` (first commit inside the challenge window)
  - [ ] Scaffold Next.js (App Router, TS strict, Tailwind, ESLint) with pnpm; add Vitest, zod, `typecheck`
  - [ ] Create `.env.example`, `docs/PROGRESS.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/post/`; fill the Commands section of CLAUDE.md
  - [ ] Verify `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`
- [ ] **0.2 Session capture (before any real coding)**
  - [ ] Install the Entire CLI (docs.entire.io/quickstart), run its Claude Code setup in the repo (`entire enable`), choose "always" to link commits to sessions. Verify with `entire checkpoint list` after a commit
  - [ ] Install DevRelay (devrelay.com, MCP server + skills) for saving a session to DEV later
  - [ ] Confirm the privacy rule: public repo means public checkpoints; no secrets in sessions
  - [ ] Timebox 20 minutes; log blockers in DECISIONS.md
- [ ] **0.3 Research: Gemma**
  - [ ] Current Gemma family and Ollama tags; pick the ~4B model that fits 16 GB RAM (do not test 12B locally)
  - [ ] Hosted Gemma option (OpenAI-compatible, free tier or credits) that offers a larger Gemma (12B or 27B): candidates Google AI Studio / Gemini API, OpenRouter, others. Record limits
  - [ ] Does the chosen Gemma accept images? (decides Phase 8)
- [ ] **0.4 Spike: Mastra (45 min, decides architecture)**
  - [ ] Minimal Mastra agent calling Ollama Gemma through an OpenAI-compatible provider
  - [ ] One tool call works (`readFile` stub) with the ~4B model
  - [ ] Structured output with a zod schema works, or a repair path is needed
  - [ ] Memory with local storage persists across two runs
  - [ ] Log results; if tool calling is unreliable on ~4B, decide: tools called by deterministic code between agent steps, or hosted larger Gemma as the agent's default
- [ ] **0.5 Spike: Entire checkpoint format (30 min)**
  - [ ] After a few commits in this repo, inspect the checkpoint data (`git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`, the stored files, `entire checkpoint explain`)
  - [ ] Document the format in DECISIONS.md: where the prompt, transcript, changed files, and any attribution data live
  - [ ] Check whether the GitHub API can read these refs on a public repo (`git/matching-refs`, trees, blobs)
- [ ] **0.6 Research: other partners (read only)**
  - [ ] Render: private services, persistent disk, instance RAM needed for ~4B Gemma on Ollama, Blueprint syntax, Deploy to Render button; claim credits at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos
  - [ ] ElevenLabs: TTS endpoint, voice IDs for two personas, speech-to-text with word timestamps; claim credits
  - [ ] Sentry: Next.js setup, AI SDK / Mastra integration for automatic LLM spans, custom span attributes, dashboards
- [ ] **0.7 Model benchmark (post material)**
  - [ ] `scripts/bench-models.ts`: same brief + question prompts, ~~10 runs each on local ~4B and hosted larger Gemma~~ 3 runs on local `gemma4:e4b` and 5 on hosted Gemma 4 31B (DECISIONS D8: CPU runs are slow; the rest moves to Phase 1 evals)
  - [ ] Record: structured output validity, median latency, question specificity (names a real file?). Tag `[POST]`
  - [ ] Set `OLLAMA_MODEL` and `HOSTED_MODEL`
- [ ] **0.8 Fixtures**
  - [ ] ~~3 public repos of different shapes (Node API, React app, Python app; include one of Wasih's if public)~~ 2 public repos of different shapes, one of Wasih's if public (DECISIONS D9)
  - [ ] Snapshot selected files into `fixtures/`
  - [ ] Plan the third fixture: this repo itself (it will have Entire checkpoints by Phase 3)

---

- **D18. Where things live.** Each checkpoint is a commit at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last 2 chars of id>/<id>`. Its tree:
  - `metadata.json`: `checkpoint_id`, `branch`, `files_touched[]`, `sessions[]` (paths to the files below), `token_usage`
  - `0/metadata.json`: `session_id`, `agent`, `model`, `created_at`, `files_touched[]`, `initial_attribution`
  - `0/prompt.txt`: the prompt of the turn that led to the commit
  - `0/transcript.jsonl`: compact transcript, one JSON object per line with `type` (`user` / `assistant`), `ts`, `content[]`
  - `0/full.jsonl`: the raw agent transcript (1.3 MB for our first one)
- **D19. Link from code to checkpoint** is the commit trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` on the normal commit. Our commits did not get an `Entire-Attribution` trailer; attribution is only inside `0/metadata.json`.
- **D20. Provenance is file-level.** `initial_attribution` has counts only (`agent_lines`, `human_added`, `human_modified`, `total_committed`, `agent_percentage`), no line ranges. So the AI-authored map is: commit -> `files_touched` + agent percentage + prompt. Line-level provenance (cut-order item 7) is not available from the checkpoint and is dropped.
- **D21. `prompt.txt` is not always a human prompt.** `[WHY]` Our first checkpoint's `prompt.txt` held a background-task notification, because that was the latest turn before the commit. The provenance reader must skip prompts that start with `<task-notification>` or other system tags and fall back to the last real `user` line in `transcript.jsonl`.
- **D22. GitHub API access works on a public repo** (verified with `gh api`): `git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints` lists the refs, `git/trees/<commit sha>?recursive=1` lists the files, `git/blobs/<sha>` returns base64 content, and the commit message from `commits/<sha>` carries the trailer. Hosted mode can use the same reader logic as local mode.
- **D23. PII redaction turned on.** The first pushed transcript contained an email address (from the session's own context) and local Windows paths. Secret redaction is on by default but PII redaction is not, so `.entire/settings.json` now sets `redaction.pii.enabled` and `email`. It only affects checkpoints written from now on.

# DECISIONS

Architecture choices and research surprises, newest at the bottom. One line of reason each. Items marked "unverified" are from docs or third parties and have not been run by us yet.

## Phase 0 (4 Oct 2026)

### Models

- **D1. Main model is hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it`, Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the laptop's MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so a local Gemma runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. Fallback: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **D2. Local Gemma is `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama**, used for the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark only. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` defaults to `hosted`; switching the env var to `ollama` still runs everything locally.
- **D3. Gemma 4, not Gemma 3.** Gemma 4 is the current family and its Ollama page lists tool calling; `gemma3:4b` has no tools support on Ollama.
- **D4. Ollama context length.** Ollama defaults to a 4k context on machines with under 24 GB of video memory, and its OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set it per request. Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (we start at 8192).
- **D5. Structured output fallback on Ollama.** If JSON through `/v1` is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field. Reason: schema-constrained output beats prompt tricks.

### Hosting

- **D6. Render: no private Ollama service** (cut-order item 3 applied up front). The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy to Render button stay. Reason: private services and disks are paid only, and an 8 GB instance price could not be confirmed.
- **D7. Keeping the free Render service awake.** A `/api/health` route pinged every 5 minutes (UptimeRobot or a cron job) stops the 15-minute idle spin-down, so a judge does not wait for a cold start. One always-on service fits in the 750 free instance hours per month.

### Scope

- **D8. Benchmark size:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; further measuring happens in Phase 1 evals. Reason: 10 CPU runs per prompt could take an hour.
- **D9. Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself (was 3 plus Viva).
- **D10. Prize categories** confirmed by Wasih from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each).
- **D11. ElevenLabs credits:** claim promo credits first; real voice only for testing and the video. Free tier is 10k credits/month; speech-to-text is reported at about 330 credits/min (unverified), so about 30 minutes.

### Tooling

- **D12. Node >= 22.13** is required by `@mastra/core` 1.74 (the laptop had 22.11.0).
- **D13. Scaffolded in a temp folder and copied in.** Reason: `create-next-app` rejects a folder name with capital letters (`Personal-viva`) and a non-empty folder.
- **D14. Next.js bundling and LibSQL.** `serverExternalPackages` lists `@libsql/client` and `@mastra/*` in `next.config.ts`, and memory is tested through a real API route in dev and in a production build. Reason: LibSQL is a native module and often breaks Next.js bundling.

### Entire

- **D15. Checkpoint storage** is one git ref per checkpoint, `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (`.entire/settings.json` shows `"type": "git-refs"`), not a branch. Format details to be confirmed on our own checkpoints in task 0.5.
- **D16. Command name:** it is `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`; there is no top-level `entire explain` in CLI 0.11.3.
- **D17. Privacy rule.** The repo is public and checkpoint refs are pushed with it, so session transcripts are public. Entire redacts detected secrets on a best-effort basis only. Keys live only in `.env` and are never pasted into a session.

### Research notes for later phases (unverified until used)

- **Mastra:** custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (docs show LM Studio only); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Structured output via `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`. Memory via `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`. Official Sentry exporter `@mastra/sentry`.
- **Entire over GitHub API:** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs (transcripts can be several MB, so use blobs, not contents).
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; speech-to-text `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` of `{text, start, end, type}`; filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs from `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default, set `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` to false; manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.chat`, `gen_ai.execute_tool`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.
- **Render:** Deploy button URL `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`; needs `render.yaml` at the repo root.

# PROGRESS

Short log, newest at the bottom. `[POST]` = material for the DEV post. `[WHY]` = a fix with an interesting reason.

## 4 Oct 2026: Phase 0.1 and 0.2 (scaffold, session capture)

- Scaffolded Next.js 16.3.8 (App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, ESLint) with pnpm; added zod 4, Vitest 5, tsx. Moved `PRD.md` and `PHASES.md` into `docs/`.
- Enabled Entire (CLI 0.11.3) for Claude Code before the first commit, so the scaffold commit is linked to its session.
- Plan review changed the architecture before any code: hosted Gemma 4 31B is the main model, local `gemma4:e4b` is for the offline clip and a small benchmark. See DECISIONS D1 to D9.
- Verified: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build` pass; first commit pushed to `main`. Not yet verified: `pnpm test` (Vitest's native binding is skipped on Node 22.11, needs >= 22.13; a winget upgrade attempt failed with installer error 1603) and an Entire checkpoint (the hooks only load in a new Claude Code session).
- Pulled `gemma4:e4b` (6.6 GB on disk, Q4_K_M, `ollama show` lists tools, vision, audio, thinking; thinking is on by default).
- `[POST]` First local speed measurement, one run of `ollama run gemma4:e4b --verbose --think=false` with a 22-token prompt on this laptop (15.9 GB RAM, MX130), Ollama's default 4096 context: cold model load 2 min 9 s, prompt read at 3.15 tokens/s, answer generated at 2.93 tokens/s (51 tokens in 17.4 s). At that prompt speed a 2,000-token repo brief would take about 10 minutes just to read in, which confirms D1. (`ollama ps` reported "266 MB, 100% GPU", which does not look right for a 6.6 GB model; not investigated.)
- `[POST]` The plan assumed Gemma 3; research found Gemma 4 is current and lists tool calling on Ollama, which Gemma 3 did not.
- `[POST]` Honest trade-off: a 16 GB laptop with an MX130 cannot run interview turns on local Gemma at a usable speed, so local mode is a privacy option, not the default. Measured numbers to follow in 0.3 and 0.7.

- **Tests cannot run on it.** Vitest's bundler requires Node 22.12 or newer, so pnpm skipped its Windows binary and `pnpm test` fails at startup.

I have not tried Mastra on 22.11, so I can't say exactly where it would break.

Forcing the missing binary in by hand and ignoring the engine warnings might get past both, but any odd failure afterwards would be hard to tell apart from a real bug. The upgrade is a few minutes and stays within Node 22, so nothing else on your machine should change.

To upgrade:

1. Close Claude Code and anything else running Node (dev servers, other terminals). My earlier attempt failed with installer error 1603, most likely because Node was in use or the admin prompt was not accepted.
2. In a fresh PowerShell window, run `winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.22` and accept the admin prompt. Or download the 22.23.2 `.msi` from nodejs.org and run it.
3. Check `node --version` shows 22.23.2, then reopen Claude Code in this folder.

After that I'll run `pnpm install` again so the skipped binary gets picked up, and carry on with the Mastra spike once the AI Studio key is in `.env`.

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code working in this repository. Read this file fully at the start of every session.

## What this project is

**Viva** is an AI interview coach for the AI-coding era. It reads your project (a GitHub repo or a local folder), finds out which parts an AI agent wrote (from Entire checkpoints, when present), and runs a mock technical interview about it, the way a placement interviewer or a final-year viva panel would. It asks follow-ups based on what you actually said, can open more files mid-interview, remembers your weak spots across sessions, coaches how you speak as well as what you say, and ends with a scored report.

One line pitch: *students now ship projects an AI half-wrote, and interviewers know it. Viva makes sure you understand what you shipped.*

Built for the DEV **Hacktoberfest 2026 Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend**. Prompt: build something with open-source AI at its core that solves a real problem for a friend. Gemma (open-weight) is the brain and must be what makes the project work.

- Builder: Abdul Wasih (final-year CSE student, strong in TypeScript)
- The friend: [FRIEND_NAME], a batchmate heading into placements (details in `docs/PRD.md` section 2)
- Requirements: `docs/PRD.md`
- Work plan and task status: `docs/PHASES.md`

## Hard deadline

**Submissions close Monday 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST (06:59 UTC).** Internal target: post published by **10:00 AM IST Monday**. The scope is ambitious on purpose. When behind, follow the **cut order** in `docs/PHASES.md` exactly; never cut the core interview, Mastra, or Entire provenance.

Challenge rules that affect the code:
- The repo and all work must start and finish inside the challenge window (from Oct 2). Any commit after the deadline must be noted in the README.
- Open-source AI must be at the core. Gemma is the brain; Mastra (open source) orchestrates; partner tools are supporting layers.

## Target prize categories (every feature should serve one)

| Category | Prize | What Viva does with it |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma (featured) | $200 | The interviewer brain: Gemma 4 31B hosted for the demo, Gemma 4 E4B on Ollama for fully offline use; the two are benchmarked against each other |
| Render (featured) | $200 | Agent frontend and API as a web service, one-click "Deploy to Render" blueprint |
| Mastra | $100 | Interviewer agent with tools (readFile, provenance lookup) and cross-session memory of weak spots |
| Entire | $100 | Viva reads Entire checkpoints to question AI-written code; the post explains Viva's own code via `entire explain` |
| ElevenLabs | $100 | Voice interviews with personas, speech-to-text with timestamps for delivery coaching |

title: serverExternalPackages
description: Opt-out specific dependencies from the Server Components bundling and use native Node.js `require`.
---

Dependencies used inside [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) will automatically be bundled by Next.js.

If a dependency is using Node.js specific features, you can choose to opt-out specific dependencies from the Server Components bundling and use native Node.js `require`.

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  serverExternalPackages: ['@acme/ui'],
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

Next.js includes a [short list of popular packages](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/lib/server-external-packages.jsonc) that currently are working on compatibility and automatically opt-ed out:

# Throwaway: start a Next.js server (dev or start), POST weak spots, restart, GET them back.
param([string]$Mode = "dev", [int]$Port = 3100)

$repo = "C:\Users\Home\Desktop\open-source\Personal-viva"
$url = "http://localhost:$Port/api/spike-memory"

function Start-Server {
  $p = Start-Process -FilePath "pnpm.cmd" -ArgumentList $Mode, "--port", $Port -WorkingDirectory $repo -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
    -RedirectStandardOutput "$env:TEMP\viva-next-$Mode.log" -RedirectStandardError "$env:TEMP\viva-next-$Mode.err"
  foreach ($i in 1..40) {
    try { Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:$Port" -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 5 | Out-Null; return $p } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
  }
  throw "server did not start"
}

function Stop-Server {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" |
    Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*Personal-viva*" -and $_.CommandLine -like "*next*" } |
    ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
}

$id = "spike-$Mode-" + (Get-Date -Format "HHmmss")
Start-Server | Out-Null
$body = @{ repoId = $id; weakSpots = @("JWT refresh flow", "database indexes") } | ConvertTo-Json
"[$Mode] POST: " + (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $url -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType "application/json" | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
Stop-Server
Start-Server | Out-Null
"[$Mode] GET after restart: " + (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$url`?repoId=$id" | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 5)
Stop-Server
"[$Mode] server errors (last lines):"
Get-Content "$env:TEMP\viva-next-$Mode.err" -Tail 8 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

input.new_string:
- **D1. Main model is hosted Gemma 4 26B** (`gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, Google AI Studio, Google's native API through Mastra's model router as `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, `thinkingLevel: "minimal"`) for development, evals and the demo.
  - Why hosted: the laptop's MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so a local Gemma runs mostly on CPU (measured: 50 to 544 s per call, see PROGRESS).
  - Why not 31B (measured 4 Oct 2026): `gemma-4-31b-it` returned HTTP 500 on 6 of 10 calls, every time a system message was sent on the OpenAI-compatible URL, and took 9 to 46 s when it did answer.
  - Why the native API and not the OpenAI-compatible URL: on the OpenAI-compatible URL thinking cannot be turned off for Gemma (`reasoning_effort` is rejected) and the thoughts leak into the answer as `<thought>` text; calls took 8 to 10 s. On the native API with minimal thinking, 26B answered a system prompt, a JSON schema and a tool call in 1.3 to 2.1 s each.
  - Why no extra package: Mastra's model router already supports `google/<model>` with an explicit `apiKey` and `providerOptions.google`, so `@ai-sdk/google` is not installed separately.
  - **Rate limits are unknown.** AI Studio does not publish free-tier limits for Gemma 4. The hosted demo therefore needs the per-IP rate limit and cached sample briefs from Phase 5. Documented fallback if Google starts failing: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free` over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit; untested by us).
- **D1a. Env variables for the hosted model:** the key stays `HOSTED_API_KEY` and the model `HOSTED_MODEL`. `HOSTED_BASE_URL` is left empty for Google and is only set for an OpenAI-compatible fallback such as OpenRouter.

input.new_string:
### Mastra spike (task 0.4, measured 4 Oct 2026 with `scripts/spikes/mastra.ts`)

- **D24. Native tool calls stay in the agent.** `readFile` was called in 5 of 5 runs on hosted 26B (median 2.9 s) and 1 of 1 on local `gemma4:e4b` (85 s). No need to drive tools from deterministic code.
- **D25. Structured output uses the schema-in-prompt mode** (`structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection: true }`), then zod. Reason: Google's native JSON-schema mode hung with no response in 4 of 15 calls (each hang lasted about 308 s before a retry succeeded, or hit our 30 s timeout), while schema-in-prompt passed 5 of 5 in the spike and 10 of 10 in the benchmark at 3 to 7 s. Small samples; Phase 1 evals will re-measure.
- **D26. Every hosted model call gets a timeout** (`abortSignal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)`) plus one retry. `[WHY]` Without it a silent hang lasts 5 minutes, which is Node's default fetch timeout.
- **D27. Local model wiring:** `model: { id: "ollama/gemma4:e4b", url: OLLAMA_BASE_URL }` works through Mastra's router (Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint). All four checks passed 1 of 1, in 50 s, 85 s, 210 s and 544 s.
- **D28. Memory:** `@mastra/memory` + `LibSQLStore` with an absolute `file:` path works inside a Next.js route handler under `next dev` and under `next build` + `next start`; a value saved before a server restart was read back after it. Weak spots are stored by plain code as thread metadata (one thread per repo), not by the model. `@libsql/client` is already on Next.js's built-in external-packages list; our `serverExternalPackages` entry is a belt-and-braces duplicate.
- **D29. Dynamic paths in routes need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`** inside `path.resolve(...)`, otherwise the production build warns that it is tracing the whole project.

### Fixtures (task 0.8)

- **D30.** Fixtures are `fixtures/vidyut-mitra` (Python backend + Next.js dashboard) and `fixtures/portfolio-new` (Vite + React), both Wasih's own public repos. Each has `SOURCE.md` (URL, commit), `FILES.tsv` (every tracked file with size) and `files/` (text files up to 70 KB; images, PDFs, fonts and lockfiles left out). `fixtures/` is excluded from typecheck, lint and tests because it is data, not our code. Neither repo has Entire checkpoints, so the provenance fixture is Viva itself (Phase 3).

# DECISIONS

Architecture choices and research surprises, newest at the bottom. One line of reason each. Items marked "unverified" are from docs or third parties and have not been run by us yet.

## Phase 0 (4 Oct 2026)

### Models

- **D1. Main model is hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it`, Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the laptop's MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so a local Gemma runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. Fallback: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **D2. Local Gemma is `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama**, used for the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark only. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` defaults to `hosted`; switching the env var to `ollama` still runs everything locally.
- **D3. Gemma 4, not Gemma 3.** Gemma 4 is the current family and its Ollama page lists tool calling; `gemma3:4b` has no tools support on Ollama.
- **D4. Ollama context length.** Ollama defaults to a 4k context on machines with under 24 GB of video memory, and its OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set it per request. Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (we start at 8192).
- **D5. Structured output fallback on Ollama.** If JSON through `/v1` is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field. Reason: schema-constrained output beats prompt tricks.

### Hosting

- **D6. Render: no private Ollama service** (cut-order item 3 applied up front). The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy to Render button stay. Reason: private services and disks are paid only, and an 8 GB instance price could not be confirmed.
- **D7. Keeping the free Render service awake.** A `/api/health` route pinged every 5 minutes (UptimeRobot or a cron job) stops the 15-minute idle spin-down, so a judge does not wait for a cold start. One always-on service fits in the 750 free instance hours per month.

### Scope

- **D8. Benchmark size:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; further measuring happens in Phase 1 evals. Reason: 10 CPU runs per prompt could take an hour.
- **D9. Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself (was 3 plus Viva).
- **D10. Prize categories** confirmed by Wasih from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each).
- **D11. ElevenLabs credits:** claim promo credits first; real voice only for testing and the video. Free tier is 10k credits/month; speech-to-text is reported at about 330 credits/min (unverified), so about 30 minutes.

### Tooling

- **D12. Node >= 22.13** is required by `@mastra/core` 1.74 (the laptop had 22.11.0).
- **D13. Scaffolded in a temp folder and copied in.** Reason: `create-next-app` rejects a folder name with capital letters (`Personal-viva`) and a non-empty folder.
- **D14. Next.js bundling and LibSQL.** `serverExternalPackages` lists `@libsql/client` and `@mastra/*` in `next.config.ts`, and memory is tested through a real API route in dev and in a production build. Reason: LibSQL is a native module and often breaks Next.js bundling.

### Entire

- **D15. Checkpoint storage** is one git ref per checkpoint, `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (`.entire/settings.json` shows `"type": "git-refs"`), not a branch. Format details to be confirmed on our own checkpoints in task 0.5.
- **D16. Command name:** it is `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`; there is no top-level `entire explain` in CLI 0.11.3.
- **D17. Privacy rule.** The repo is public and checkpoint refs are pushed with it, so session transcripts are public. Entire redacts detected secrets on a best-effort basis only. Keys live only in `.env` and are never pasted into a session.

### Entire checkpoint format (task 0.5, verified on this repo's first checkpoint, CLI 0.11.3)

- **D18. Where things live.** Each checkpoint is a commit at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last 2 chars of id>/<id>`. Its tree:
  - `metadata.json`: `checkpoint_id`, `branch`, `files_touched[]`, `sessions[]` (paths to the files below), `token_usage`
  - `0/metadata.json`: `session_id`, `agent`, `model`, `created_at`, `files_touched[]`, `initial_attribution`
  - `0/prompt.txt`: the prompt of the turn that led to the commit
  - `0/transcript.jsonl`: compact transcript, one JSON object per line with `type` (`user` / `assistant`), `ts`, `content[]`
  - `0/full.jsonl`: the raw agent transcript (1.3 MB for our first one)
- **D19. Link from code to checkpoint** is the commit trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` on the normal commit. Our commits did not get an `Entire-Attribution` trailer; attribution is only inside `0/metadata.json`.
- **D20. Provenance is file-level.** `initial_attribution` has counts only (`agent_lines`, `human_added`, `human_modified`, `total_committed`, `agent_percentage`), no line ranges. So the AI-authored map is: commit -> `files_touched` + agent percentage + prompt. Line-level provenance (cut-order item 7) is not available from the checkpoint and is dropped.
- **D21. `prompt.txt` is not always a human prompt.** `[WHY]` Our first checkpoint's `prompt.txt` held a background-task notification, because that was the latest turn before the commit. The provenance reader must skip prompts that start with `<task-notification>` or other system tags and fall back to the last real `user` line in `transcript.jsonl`.
- **D22. GitHub API access works on a public repo** (verified with `gh api`): `git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints` lists the refs, `git/trees/<commit sha>?recursive=1` lists the files, `git/blobs/<sha>` returns base64 content, and the commit message from `commits/<sha>` carries the trailer. Hosted mode can use the same reader logic as local mode.
- **D23. PII redaction turned on.** The first pushed transcript contained an email address (from the session's own context) and local Windows paths. Secret redaction is on by default but PII redaction is not, so `.entire/settings.json` now sets `redaction.pii.enabled` and `email`. It only affects checkpoints written from now on.

### Research notes for later phases (unverified until used)

- **Mastra:** custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (docs show LM Studio only); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Structured output via `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`. Memory via `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`. Official Sentry exporter `@mastra/sentry`.
- **Entire over GitHub API:** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs (transcripts can be several MB, so use blobs, not contents).
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; speech-to-text `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` of `{text, start, end, type}`; filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs from `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default, set `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` to false; manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.chat`, `gen_ai.execute_tool`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.
- **Render:** Deploy button URL `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`; needs `render.yaml` at the repo root.

- **D1a. Env variables for the hosted model:** the key stays `HOSTED_API_KEY` and the model `HOSTED_MODEL`. `HOSTED_BASE_URL` is left empty for Google and is only set for an OpenAI-compatible fallback such as OpenRouter.
- **D2. Local Gemma is `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama**, used for the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark only. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` defaults to `hosted`; switching the env var to `ollama` still runs everything locally.
- **D3. Gemma 4, not Gemma 3.** Gemma 4 is the current family and its Ollama page lists tool calling; `gemma3:4b` has no tools support on Ollama.
- **D4. Ollama context length.** Ollama defaults to a 4k context on machines with under 24 GB of video memory, and its OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set it per request. Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (we start at 8192).
- **D5. Structured output fallback on Ollama.** If JSON through `/v1` is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field. Reason: schema-constrained output beats prompt tricks.

### Hosting

- **D6. Render: no private Ollama service** (cut-order item 3 applied up front). The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy to Render button stay. Reason: private services and disks are paid only, and an 8 GB instance price could not be confirmed.
- **D7. Keeping the free Render service awake.** A `/api/health` route pinged every 5 minutes (UptimeRobot or a cron job) stops the 15-minute idle spin-down, so a judge does not wait for a cold start. One always-on service fits in the 750 free instance hours per month.

### Scope

- **D8. Benchmark size:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; further measuring happens in Phase 1 evals. Reason: 10 CPU runs per prompt could take an hour.
- **D9. Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself (was 3 plus Viva).
- **D10. Prize categories** confirmed by Wasih from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each).
- **D11. ElevenLabs credits:** claim promo credits first; real voice only for testing and the video. Free tier is 10k credits/month; speech-to-text is reported at about 330 credits/min (unverified), so about 30 minutes.

### Tooling

- **D12. Node >= 22.13** is required by `@mastra/core` 1.74 (the laptop had 22.11.0).
- **D13. Scaffolded in a temp folder and copied in.** Reason: `create-next-app` rejects a folder name with capital letters (`Personal-viva`) and a non-empty folder.
- **D14. Next.js bundling and LibSQL.** `serverExternalPackages` lists `@libsql/client` and `@mastra/*` in `next.config.ts`, and memory is tested through a real API route in dev and in a production build. Reason: LibSQL is a native module and often breaks Next.js bundling.

### Entire

- **D15. Checkpoint storage** is one git ref per checkpoint, `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (`.entire/settings.json` shows `"type": "git-refs"`), not a branch. Format details to be confirmed on our own checkpoints in task 0.5.
- **D16. Command name:** it is `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`; there is no top-level `entire explain` in CLI 0.11.3.
- **D17. Privacy rule.** The repo is public and checkpoint refs are pushed with it, so session transcripts are public. Entire redacts detected secrets on a best-effort basis only. Keys live only in `.env` and are never pasted into a session.

### Entire checkpoint format (task 0.5, verified on this repo's first checkpoint, CLI 0.11.3)

- **D18. Where things live.** Each checkpoint is a commit at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last 2 chars of id>/<id>`. Its tree:
  - `metadata.json`: `checkpoint_id`, `branch`, `files_touched[]`, `sessions[]` (paths to the files below), `token_usage`
  - `0/metadata.json`: `session_id`, `agent`, `model`, `created_at`, `files_touched[]`, `initial_attribution`
  - `0/prompt.txt`: the prompt of the turn that led to the commit
  - `0/transcript.jsonl`: compact transcript, one JSON object per line with `type` (`user` / `assistant`), `ts`, `content[]`
  - `0/full.jsonl`: the raw agent transcript (1.3 MB for our first one)
- **D19. Link from code to checkpoint** is the commit trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` on the normal commit. Our commits did not get an `Entire-Attribution` trailer; attribution is only inside `0/metadata.json`.
- **D20. Provenance is file-level.** `initial_attribution` has counts only (`agent_lines`, `human_added`, `human_modified`, `total_committed`, `agent_percentage`), no line ranges. So the AI-authored map is: commit -> `files_touched` + agent percentage + prompt. Line-level provenance (cut-order item 7) is not available from the checkpoint and is dropped.
- **D21. `prompt.txt` is not always a human prompt.** `[WHY]` Our first checkpoint's `prompt.txt` held a background-task notification, because that was the latest turn before the commit. The provenance reader must skip prompts that start with `<task-notification>` or other system tags and fall back to the last real `user` line in `transcript.jsonl`.
- **D22. GitHub API access works on a public repo** (verified with `gh api`): `git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints` lists the refs, `git/trees/<commit sha>?recursive=1` lists the files, `git/blobs/<sha>` returns base64 content, and the commit message from `commits/<sha>` carries the trailer. Hosted mode can use the same reader logic as local mode.
- **D23. PII redaction turned on.** The first pushed transcript contained an email address (from the session's own context) and local Windows paths. Secret redaction is on by default but PII redaction is not, so `.entire/settings.json` now sets `redaction.pii.enabled` and `email`. It only affects checkpoints written from now on.

### Research notes for later phases (unverified until used)

- **Mastra:** custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (docs show LM Studio only); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Structured output via `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`. Memory via `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`. Official Sentry exporter `@mastra/sentry`.
- **Entire over GitHub API:** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs (transcripts can be several MB, so use blobs, not contents).
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; speech-to-text `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` of `{text, start, end, type}`; filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs from `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default, set `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` to false; manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.chat`, `gen_ai.execute_tool`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.
- **Render:** Deploy button URL `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`; needs `render.yaml` at the repo root.

- Why the native API and not the OpenAI-compatible URL: on the OpenAI-compatible URL thinking cannot be turned off for Gemma (`reasoning_effort` is rejected) and the thoughts leak into the answer as `<thought>` text; calls took 8 to 10 s. On the native API with minimal thinking, 26B answered a system prompt, a JSON schema and a tool call in 1.3 to 2.1 s each.
- Why no extra package: Mastra's model router already supports `google/<model>` with an explicit `apiKey` and `providerOptions.google`, so `@ai-sdk/google` is not installed separately.

- **Rate limits are unknown.** AI Studio does not publish free-tier limits for Gemma 4. The hosted demo therefore needs the per-IP rate limit and cached sample briefs from Phase 5. Documented fallback if Google starts failing: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free` over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit; untested by us).
